claim: Regulatory T (Treg) cells suppress autoimmunity and other inflammatory states.
source: Regulatory T (Treg) cells, which suppress autoimmunity and other inflammatory states, are characterized by a distinct set of genetic elements controlling their gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a defining characteristic of Treg cells.

claim: Treg cells are characterized by a distinct set of genetic elements controlling their gene expression.
source: Regulatory T (Treg) cells, which suppress autoimmunity and other inflammatory states, are characterized by a distinct set of genetic elements controlling their gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a fundamental property of Treg cells.

claim: A small set of regulatory elements specify the Treg lineage.
source: Our findings suggest that a small set of regulatory elements specify the Treg lineage and that genetic variation in Treg cell-specific enhancers may alter Treg cell function contributing to polygenic disease.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on the conservation analysis performed in the study.

claim: Genetic variation in Treg cell-specific enhancers may alter Treg cell function contributing to polygenic disease.
source: Our findings suggest that a small set of regulatory elements specify the Treg lineage and that genetic variation in Treg cell-specific enhancers may alter Treg cell function contributing to polygenic disease.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on disease association analysis.

claim: The majority of protein-coding genome sequence is under constraint due to the cost of deleterious mutational perturbations in protein function.
source: Since the majority of protein-coding genome sequence is under constraint, due to the cost of deleterious mutational perturbations in protein function, changes in non-coding regulatory portions of the genome are thought to serve as a major source of evolutionary innovation and substrates for selection (King and Wilson, 1975; Schmidt et al., 2010; Goncalves et al., 2012; Ward and Kellis, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Changes in non-coding regulatory portions of the genome serve as a major source of evolutionary innovation and substrates for selection.
source: Since the majority of protein-coding genome sequence is under constraint, due to the cost of deleterious mutational perturbations in protein function, changes in non-coding regulatory portions of the genome are thought to serve as a major source of evolutionary innovation and substrates for selection (King and Wilson, 1975; Schmidt et al., 2010; Goncalves et al., 2012; Ward and Kellis, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Treg cell differentiation and function is controlled by the lineage specification factor Foxp3.
source: Treg cell differentiation and function is controlled by a late-acting lineage specification factor Foxp3, which is induced upon signaling through T cell (TCR) and cytokine receptors (Hill et al., 2007; Ohkura et al., 2012; Samstein et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Foxp3 is induced upon signaling through T cell (TCR) and cytokine receptors.
source: Treg cell differentiation and function is controlled by a late-acting lineage specification factor Foxp3, which is induced upon signaling through T cell (TCR) and cytokine receptors (Hill et al., 2007; Ohkura et al., 2012; Samstein et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Genetic Foxp3 deficiency or elimination of Treg cells in mice results in lymphoproliferation and myeloproliferation leading to widespread fatal autoimmune lesions.
source: Genetic Foxp3 deficiency or elimination of Treg cells in mice results in lymphoproliferation and myeloproliferation leading to widespread fatal autoimmune lesions largely driven by activation of 'self'-, commensal microbiota-, and food-derived antigen-reactive CD4 T cells (Brunkow et al., 2001; Fontenot et al., 2003; Khattri et al., 2003; Kim et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Human IPEX patients with loss-of-function Foxp3 mutations present with neonatal diabetes, thyroiditis, autoimmune anemia and neutropenia, autoimmune hepatitis, exudative dermatitis, enteropathies, and hyper-IgE syndrome.
source: Human IPEX patients with loss-of-function Foxp3 mutations and congenital Treg cell deficiency present with neonatal diabetes, thyroiditis, autoimmune anemia and neutropenia, autoimmune hepatitis, exudative dermatitis, enteropathies, and hyper-IgE syndrome (Bennett et al., 2001; Torgerson and Ochs, 2007; Verbsky and Chatila, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Approximately 31,000 H3K27 acetylation peaks were observed across the genome in CD4+ T-cell subsets.
source: We observed ∼31,000 H3K27 acetylation peaks across the genome in CD4+ T-cell subsets, which we stratified by reads aligned per million (RPM) in each cell population.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the ChIP-seq experiments performed in the study.

claim: Approximately 27,000 orthologous regulatory elements were identified between human and mouse.
source: Genome-wide comparison between human and mouse identified ∼27,000 orthologous regulatory elements (Figure 1F,G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is a direct result from the conservation analysis performed in the study.

claim: The level of H3K27ac at conserved genetic elements was highly correlated (r = 0.48) between human and mouse.
source: The level of H3K27ac at conserved genetic elements was highly correlated (r = 0.48), with a plurality of shared elements being weakly active in both organisms (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the conservation analysis shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Very few regulatory elements are Treg cell-specific in both human and mouse species.
source: Intriguingly, while the genome-wide epigenetically active landscape was similar in human and mouse, quantification of cell lineage specificity revealed that very few of the elements are Treg cell-specific in both species (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the lineage-specificity analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Conserved Treg lineage-specific regulatory elements include those near FOXP3, IL2RA (CD25), CTLA4, IKZF2 (HELIOS), IL2RB, DUSP4, BLIMP1, TNFRSF8, TNFRSF9, CCR8, and LRRC32.
source: Specifically, we were able to identify conserved epigenetic modifications at a small set of regulatory elements, which could be assigned to a handful of genes, including FOXP3, IL2RA (CD25), CTLA4, IKZF2 (HELIOS), IL2RB, DUSP4, BLIMP1, TNFRSF8, TNFRSF9, CCR8, and LRRC32 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is a direct result from the conservation analysis of lineage-specific elements.

claim: There was greater statistical enrichment for conserved loci downregulated in a Treg-specific fashion, including IL7R (CD127), IL2, PDE3B, LEF1, IL21, PDE7A, TNFSF8, and THEMIS.
source: Interestingly, there was greater statistical enrichment for conserved loci downregulated in a Treg-specific fashion, which included IL7R (CD127), IL2, PDE3B, LEF1, IL21, PDE7A, TNFSF8, and THEMIS.
evidence: This is a result from the statistical analysis of conserved downregulated elements.

claim: Organism-specific cell lineage-associated variation in H3K27 acetylation correlated with organism-specific gene expression changes.
source: We also observed that organism-specific cell lineage-associated variation in H3K27 acetylation correlated with organism-specific gene expression changes (Figure 2D,E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a result from the integrated analysis of epigenetic and gene expression data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Many Foxp3-bound loci were genetically conserved and bound in both human and mouse organisms.
source: We quantified Foxp3 binding in human and murine Treg cells and found that many Foxp3-bound loci were genetically conserved and bound in both organisms (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B; Supplementary files 7-9).
evidence: This is a direct result from the Foxp3 ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Conserved Foxp3 binding was associated with decreased H3K27ac in both human and mouse.
source: We found that conserved Foxp3 binding was associated with decreased H3K27ac in both human and mouse (Figure 3C,D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a result from the integrated analysis of Foxp3 binding and H3K27ac shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: At human- or mouse species-specific Foxp3-bound sites, H3K27ac was decreased exclusively in the corresponding organism.
source: Importantly, at human- or mouse species-specific Foxp3-bound sites, H3K27ac was decreased exclusively in the corresponding organism (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of species-specific Foxp3 binding shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Species-specific Foxp3 occupancy at genetically conserved loci was associated with presence of forkhead DNA-binding motifs at the corresponding Foxp3-bound sites.
source: Species-specific Foxp3 occupancy at genetically conserved loci was also associated with presence of forkhead DNA-binding motifs at the corresponding Foxp3-bound sites (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a result from the motif analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Approximately 80,000 DHSs contained at least 1 polymorphism cataloged in the single nucleotide polymorphism database (dbSNP).
source: We examined a narrow genomic window (150 bp) at each of the ∼85,000 DHSs to find that ∼80,000 contained at least 1 polymorphism cataloged in the single nucleotide polymorphism database (dbSNP) and that ∼45,000 of these contained polymorphisms with significant (>0.05) minor allele frequency (MAF) in at least one of the thousand genome project (1000G) populations (Figure 4A; 'Materials and methods'; Supplementary file 13).
evidence: This is a direct result from the polymorphism analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Approximately 45,000 DHSs contained polymorphisms with significant (>0.05) minor allele frequency (MAF) in at least one of the thousand genome project (1000G) populations.
source: We examined a narrow genomic window (150 bp) at each of the ∼85,000 DHSs to find that ∼80,000 contained at least 1 polymorphism cataloged in the single nucleotide polymorphism database (dbSNP) and that ∼45,000 of these contained polymorphisms with significant (>0.05) minor allele frequency (MAF) in at least one of the thousand genome project (1000G) populations (Figure 4A; 'Materials and methods'; Supplementary file 13).
evidence: This is a direct result from the polymorphism analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Genetically conserved elements had decreased maximum MAF relative to expected frequency.
source: Consistent with evolutionary constraint, genetically conserved elements had decreased maximum MAF relative to expected frequency (Figure 4B; 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a result from the conservation analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The activated Treg cell-specific expression of ENTPD1 is associated with a haplotype represented by single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs1342790.
source: For example, the Treg cell lineage-specific enhancer containing the single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2882971 at the ENTPD1 locus demonstrated genetic association with H3K27ac levels across individuals and in an allele-specific manner in a given individual (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C which demonstrates the association between genotype and H3K27ac at the ENTPD1 locus.

claim: The ENTPD1 locus demonstrates genetic association with H3K27ac levels across individuals and in an allele-specific manner.
source: For example, the Treg cell lineage-specific enhancer containing the single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2882971 at the ENTPD1 locus demonstrated genetic association with H3K27ac levels across individuals and in an allele-specific manner in a given individual (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C and confirmed by meta-analysis in Figure 4D.

claim: ENTPD1 RNA and protein expression is associated with a strong cis-eQTL.
source: This is consistent with previous reports showing ENTPD1 RNA and protein expression association with a strong cis-eQTL (Orrù et al., 2013; Ferraro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Most disease-predisposing susceptibility loci reside in non-coding portions of the genome.
source: Furthermore, recent findings from genome-wide association (GWA) studies have revealed that most disease-predisposing susceptibility loci reside in non-coding portions of the genome (Welter et al., 2014; Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the majority of polygenic disease is in fact due to variation in transcriptional control rather than protein structure and function.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The majority of polygenic disease is due to variation in transcriptional control rather than protein structure and function.
source: Furthermore, recent findings from genome-wide association (GWA) studies have revealed that most disease-predisposing susceptibility loci reside in non-coding portions of the genome (Welter et al., 2014; Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the majority of polygenic disease is in fact due to variation in transcriptional control rather than protein structure and function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that most disease loci are non-coding.

claim: Active chromatin is enriched for variants that contribute to polygenic diseases, including autoimmunity.
source: Recent studies have also found that active chromatin is enriched for variants that contribute to polygenic diseases, including autoimmunity (Maurano et al., 2012; Trynka et al., 2013; Farh et al., 2014), and that these variants can alter transcriptional regulator protein-DNA interactions, resulting in differential gene expression (Ferraro et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2014; Ye et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Variants in active chromatin can alter transcriptional regulator protein-DNA interactions, resulting in differential gene expression.
source: Recent studies have also found that active chromatin is enriched for variants that contribute to polygenic diseases, including autoimmunity (Maurano et al., 2012; Trynka et al., 2013; Farh et al., 2014), and that these variants can alter transcriptional regulator protein-DNA interactions, resulting in differential gene expression (Ferraro et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2014; Ye et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The CTLA4 locus harbors a risk allele for multiple autoimmune disorders, including rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes (T1D), Graves' disease, and systemic lupus erythematosus.
source: One such strictly Treg cell-specific epigenetic element was found at the CTLA4 locus, which harbors a risk allele for multiple autoimmune disorders, including rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes (T1D), Graves' disease, and systemic lupus erythematosus (Scalapino and Daikh, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The most disease-associated variants at the CTLA4 locus, represented by rs2882971, lie within Treg cell-specific enhancers that are epigenetically conserved and lineage-specific in both human and mouse.
source: While early GWA genotyping approaches were too coarse to localize the causative polymorphism, fine mapping by the ImmunoChip across a large case–control T1D cohort demonstrated that the most disease-associated variants, represented by rs2882971, lie within Treg cell-specific enhancers that are epigenetically conserved and lineage-specific in both human and mouse (Figure 5A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) (Onengut-Gumuscu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A non-coding CTLA4 polymorphism in linkage disequilibrium with rs2882971 (rs3087243) influences the CTLA4 splice form dosage, with disease-predisposing variants decreasing the soluble isoform that is expressed in Treg cells.
source: Functional relevance of a non-coding CTLA4 polymorphism in linkage disequilibrium with rs2882971 (rs3087243) has been experimentally validated as influencing the CTLA4 splice form dosage, with disease-predisposing variants decreasing the soluble isoform that is expressed in Treg cells (Ueda et al., 2003; Atabani et al., 2005; Gerold et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Dozens of Treg cell lineage-specific epigenetic elements harbor genetic variation associated with polygenic autoimmune disease such as T1D.
source: We identified dozens of Treg cell lineage-specific epigenetic elements that harbor genetic variation associated with and potentially contributing to polygenic autoimmune disease such as T1D (Figure 5B,C; 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a result from the disease association analysis shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Many autoimmune disease risk alleles were in LD or were proximal to genes with epigenetically conserved Treg lineage-specific elements.
source: Analysis of these risk alleles revealed that many were in LD or were proximal to genes with epigenetically conserved Treg lineage-specific elements (Figure 5D), suggesting that these elements have important conserved function.
evidence: This is a result from the disease association analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: An aggregate GWAS data set of metabolic (e.g., type 2 diabetes) and psychiatric disorders lacked disease associations in conserved Treg lineage-specific elements.
source: In contrast, an aggregate GWAS data set of metabolic (e.g., type 2 diabetes) and psychiatric disorders lacked disease associations in conserved Treg lineage-specific elements.
evidence: This is a result from the disease association analysis comparing autoimmune vs metabolic/psychiatric disorders.

claim: Psychiatric disorders risk-alleles were generally localized in non-conserved genetic elements.
source: Furthermore, psychiatric disorders risk-alleles were generally localized in non-conserved genetic elements, which is consistent with recent reports finding substantial human-specific genetic diversity in cognition-associated genes in comparison to recent evolutionary ancestors (Ogawa and Vallender, 2014).
evidence: This is a result from the disease association analysis and is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Less than 10% of lineage-specific epigenetic elements were lineage-specific in both mouse and human.
source: In our comparison of Treg and effector T-cell lineages, we found that ∼85% of regulatory elements were genetically conserved and epigenetically active in both human and mouse, ∼1–2% were lineage-specific in human or mouse, and <0.1% were lineage-specific in both human and mouse. This indicates that of those elements that are specific to the Treg lineage, less than 10% were lineage-specific in both mouse and human.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the conservation analysis.

claim: Approximately 85% of regulatory elements were genetically conserved and epigenetically active in both human and mouse.
source: In our comparison of Treg and effector T-cell lineages, we found that ∼85% of regulatory elements were genetically conserved and epigenetically active in both human and mouse, ∼1–2% were lineage-specific in human or mouse, and <0.1% were lineage-specific in both human and mouse.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the conservation analysis.

claim: Approximately 1-2% of regulatory elements were lineage-specific in human or mouse.
source: In our comparison of Treg and effector T-cell lineages, we found that ∼85% of regulatory elements were genetically conserved and epigenetically active in both human and mouse, ∼1–2% were lineage-specific in human or mouse, and <0.1% were lineage-specific in both human and mouse.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the conservation analysis.

claim: Less than 0.1% of regulatory elements were lineage-specific in both human and mouse.
source: In our comparison of Treg and effector T-cell lineages, we found that ∼85% of regulatory elements were genetically conserved and epigenetically active in both human and mouse, ∼1–2% were lineage-specific in human or mouse, and <0.1% were lineage-specific in both human and mouse.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the conservation analysis.

claim: Lineage specification programs may be dependent on but a few immutable genetic regulatory elements, while tolerating considerable epigenetic variation at numerous additional organism-specific lineage-specific elements.
source: These findings suggest that lineage specification programs may be dependent on but a few immutable genetic regulatory elements, while tolerating considerable epigenetic variation at numerous additional organism-specific lineage-specific elements.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conservation analysis results.

claim: Limited turnover of regulatory elements that are lineage-specific in both mouse and human confirms the unique importance of these individual regulatory elements.
source: Given previous findings regarding the extensive turnover of DNA elements in genome-wide regulatory networks (Stergachis et al., 2014; Vierstra et al., 2014), it is noteworthy that we found limited turnover of regulatory elements that are lineage-specific in both mouse and human. This confirms the unique importance of these individual regulatory elements.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conservation analysis results and comparison to previous literature.

claim: The Foxp3-mediated transcriptional control program was subject to forkhead-binding motif 'turnover' that was associated with functional consequences.
source: Furthermore, we found that the Foxp3-mediated transcriptional control program was subject to forkhead-binding motif 'turnover' that was associated with functional consequences.
evidence: This is a result from the Foxp3 binding and motif analysis.

claim: Regulatory elements with conserved lineage-specific epigenetic activity were associated with far more pronounced regulation of Treg cell lineage-specific gene expression.
source: While these organism-specific elements contributed to gene regulation, the regulatory elements with conserved lineage-specific epigenetic activity were associated with far more pronounced regulation of Treg cell lineage-specific gene expression.
evidence: This is a result from the integrated analysis of epigenetic and gene expression data.

claim: Autoimmune diabetes development is impacted most significantly by HLA risk alleles.
source: For instance, it is reasonable to consider that autoimmune diabetes development is impacted most significantly by HLA risk alleles (Wong et al., 2004; Stadinski et al., 2010), and to a lesser degree by other susceptibility determinants including potentially compromised Treg cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The majority of polymorphisms exist as broad haplotype blocks that cannot be perfectly resolved to a single or several lineage-specific enhancers.
source: Though, we observed statistical enrichment of risk alleles near Treg cell enhancers, it is worth noting that the majority of polymorphisms exist as broad haplotype blocks that cannot be perfectly resolved to a single or several lineage-specific enhancers.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged in the discussion.

claim: During cellular differentiation, only a handful of epigenetic elements implement the core transcriptional program that underlies establishment of a differentiated Treg cell identity and function.
source: Our study suggests that the vast majority of Treg cell lineage-specific elements are not conserved between mice and humans suggesting that during cellular differentiation, only a handful of epigenetic elements implement the core transcriptional program that underlies establishment of a differentiated Treg cell identity and function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conservation analysis results.

claim: Disease-associated polymorphisms clustered at genic loci containing core lineage-specific epigenetic elements.
source: In support of this model, disease-associated polymorphisms clustered at genic loci containing core lineage-specific epigenetic elements.
evidence: This is a result from the disease association analysis.

claim: Most Treg lineage-specific regulatory elements were lineage-specific only in human and could harbor extensive natural genetic variation that could influence transcription, alter cellular function, and contribute to polygenic disease.
source: Nevertheless, most Treg lineage-specific regulatory elements were lineage-specific only in human and could harbor extensive natural genetic variation that could influence transcription, alter cellular function, and contribute to polygenic disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conservation and polymorphism analysis results.

claim: High-resolution epigenetic and genome-wide genetic disease association data enabled localization of disease-risk linked polymorphisms to regulatory loci that are exclusively epigenetically active in Treg cells.
source: This orthogonal high-resolution epigenetic and genetic analysis enabled characterization of disease-predisposing genetic variation associated with Treg-specific enhancers, and therefore, implicated Treg cells in complex autoimmune disease.
evidence: This is a summary of the approach and findings of the study.

claim: The analysis implicated Treg cells in complex autoimmune disease.
source: This orthogonal high-resolution epigenetic and genetic analysis enabled characterization of disease-predisposing genetic variation associated with Treg-specific enhancers, and therefore, implicated Treg cells in complex autoimmune disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the disease association analysis.

claim: Human CD4+ T cells were isolated from peripheral blood of individual anonymous human donors using negative selection.
source: CD4+ T cells were enriched through negative selection with RosetteSep antibody cocktails (Stem Cell Technologies #15062, Vancouver, BC Canada).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Resting and activated Treg and effector CD4+ T-cell subsets were purified using FACS sorting based on expression of CD25 and CD45RO with >97–99% purity.
source: Isolated CD4+ T cells were stained for CD3 (PE-TexasRed, Invitrogen #MHCD0317, Waltham, MA, United States), CD4 (APC-eFluor 780, eBioscience #47-0049-42, San Diego, CA, United States), CD45RA (APC, BioLegend #304112), CD45RO (PE-Cy7, BioLegend #304230), and CD25 (PE, BioLegend #302606), and resting and activated Treg and effector CD4+ T-cell subsets were purified on a BD Biosciences Aria2 fluorescent cell sorter.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study, with purity mentioned in the text.

claim: DT treatment resulted in transient ablation of Treg cells and systemic inflammation.
source: DT treatment resulted in transient ablation of Treg cells and systemic inflammation.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods and their effects.

claim: A total of 16 human cell samples from 7 donors were analyzed, including 7 aTreg, 4 rTreg, 2 Teff, 2 Tmem, and 1 Tn samples.
source: In total, we analyzed 16 human cell samples (7 donors: 7 aTreg, 4 rTreg, 2 Teff, 2 Tmem, and 1 Tn samples) and 10 murine samples (2 aTreg, 4 rTreg, 2 Teff, and 4 Tn biological replicates independently isolated from different mice).
evidence: This is a description of the sample sizes used in the study.

claim: A total of 10 mouse cell samples were analyzed, including 2 aTreg, 4 rTreg, 2 Teff, and 4 Tn biological replicates.
source: In total, we analyzed 16 human cell samples (7 donors: 7 aTreg, 4 rTreg, 2 Teff, 2 Tmem, and 1 Tn samples) and 10 murine samples (2 aTreg, 4 rTreg, 2 Teff, and 4 Tn biological replicates independently isolated from different mice).
evidence: This is a description of the sample sizes used in the study.

claim: ChIP-seq analysis of H3K27Ac was performed using the H3K27Ac-specific antibody (Abcam ab4729) raised against the conserved acetylated epitope 'LATKAARKSAPA'.
source: ChIP was performed using the H3K27Ac-specific antibody (Abcam ab4729, Cambridge, United Kingdom) raised against the conserved acetylated epitope 'LATKAARKSAPA'.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Peaks were called using MACSv2 using default parameters and a permissive threshold for total peak count (p < 0.0001).
source: Peaks were called using MACSv2 using default parameters and a permissive threshold for total peak count (p < 0.0001).
evidence: This is a description of the computational methods used in the study.

claim: The LRRC32 locus contains multiple epigenetically active regulatory elements that are conserved and Treg lineage-specific in mouse and human.
source: For instance, the LRRC32 locus, which encodes the GARP protein that acts as a functionally important marker of activated Treg cells in humans (Wang et al., 2009), has multiple regulatory elements that are genetically conserved, epigenetically conserved, and only active in the Treg cell lineage (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A and described in the text.

claim: LRRC32 encodes the GARP protein that acts as a functionally important marker of activated Treg cells in humans.
source: For instance, the LRRC32 locus, which encodes the GARP protein that acts as a functionally important marker of activated Treg cells in humans (Wang et al., 2009), has multiple regulatory elements that are genetically conserved, epigenetically conserved, and only active in the Treg cell lineage (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Approximately 85,000 DHSs were identified in CD4+ T-cell populations.
source: We examined a narrow genomic window (150 bp) at each of the ∼85,000 DHSs
evidence: This is a direct result from the DNase-seq analysis.

claim: Correlation across mouse biological replicates was r > 0.99.
source: Correlation across mouse biological replicates was r > 0.99 and between human donors r > 0.94, indicating that the observed conservation and lack thereof are reflective of biology and not technical/replicate reproducibility (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1K.

claim: Correlation between human donors was r > 0.94.
source: Correlation across mouse biological replicates was r > 0.99 and between human donors r > 0.94, indicating that the observed conservation and lack thereof are reflective of biology and not technical/replicate reproducibility (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1K.
